_comment: Scenario-staged routing demo beside impassable terrain: a brittle player cavalry unit (60 mounts at morale 0.5) starts just west of the default hill (Rect2(1150, 380, 250, 200)) and holds there until an enemy cavalry charge from its WESTERN flank comes in. Both units stand clear of the hill for the whole clip: the router's block is 280 wu wide, so its centre at x=960 keeps its eastern file 50 wu clear of the hill's west face. The pursuer's target sits 190 wu west of the hill and 40 wu below its bottom edge, so its leg is clear of the hill and it charges straight east. Measured with a 2-tick dense state dump: the router holds at its spawn through tick 120, the charge makes contact at tick 159 and drives the router back about 60 wu west, the two fight one unbroken melee, and the router routs at tick 344. The rout keeps the router's slot grid where its men stood when it broke (#1765), and the router is carried east along the pursuer's front while the pursuer is still on it (about (1044, 657) at tick 440, (1085, 622) at tick 492, its men up against the hill's west face but none inside it), then flees north-west and north (about (967, 474) at tick 560, (979, 237) at tick 680), every man clear of the hill, and rallies at tick 704 (ROUTING at 703, IDLE at 704) at about (976, 174), inside the clip (it ends at tick 720). The rally turns its heading by up to a quarter-turn so its ranks lie square across it (-91 to -19 degrees), and it pulls up with its men in step (anchor about (974, 154) at tick 710, still coasting at about (972, 123) when the clip ends); its men arrive at the rally still off their own slots after the interleaved fight (#1725), 86.4 wu on average at tick 703 (298.6 on main e81ea9fa). The pursuer's facing turns smoothly through the charge, with no snap larger than 20 degrees between 2-tick samples. This scenario does NOT show a rout detouring around the hill: the router's flight never meets it. The 'stands and fights when genuinely trapped' case is covered by test_trapped_routing_unit_fights_instead_of_fleeing. No player input needed; the scenario + seed make the clash deterministic. After the rout the router streams out through the pursuer's deep column: the pursuer holds its facing (26 degrees at tick 440) and its slot grid while the router is among its ranks. At tick 483, as the router leaves it, its facing snaps 35 degrees to -13 (under the 75 degree threshold above which a re-face turns in place, so the snap is not folded into its grid) and its mean body-to-slot gap jumps from 65.4 to 143.0 wu; at tick 504 it re-faces 167 degrees (folded in, the gap unchanged) and stays near the hill's south-west corner (anchor about (1094, 688) at tick 720) rather than riding north after it. A 2-tick scan from the divergence (tick 343) reads the pursuer's sustained shape residual at 102.6 wu against the 30 wu threshold (declared below); on main e81ea9fa it read 13.3 wu, and on main fa76accc, where the grid swung round with the facing and the anchor backed away to the south-east, 142.2 wu (#1757). Before the charge came straight in (rout at tick 469), the same scan from the rout read 75.4 wu: the straight charge did not cause the deformation. The declared checks pin the router's story beats with sparse post-rout samples (400, 560, 680, the rally at 703/704, and 710) rather than sampling the gallop densely. The router's own scramble (judged only on the 16 ticks after its rally) is declared below as an exemption rather than sampled around.
